description: Por cierto, un gato vino a la oficina a hacer una entrevista de trabajo. No lo contratamos. Vale que estamos hasta arriba, pero un gato... no es mas que un gato. Pero la verdad es que me siento afortunado si veo uno en la oficina o por la calle. ¿Tú no?
summary: Martial Outpost is an interactive resource-management and decision-making educational game built in Godot to address the NASA Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. Set in a human colony on Mars, the game places children in command of a Red Planet outpost where every choice has immediate consequences for colonist survival. Through an intuitive choice-driven mechanic, players must keep critical Energy, Food, and Water meters in the positive while preventing Radiation—one of the deadliest hazards on the Martian surface—from reaching dangerous thresholds. As they manage the colony, children naturally learn real scientific terminology used by NASA in Mars exploration (such as dust demons, Fission Surface Power and radiation), turning complex planetary engineering challenges into a fun, accessible, and memorable experience.
details:
Do you have what it takes to keep a colony alive on the Red Planet? Living on Mars requires making tough calls in a matter of seconds. Without a thick atmosphere or global magnetic field to shield the surface, every watt of solar power, every liter of recycled water, and every layer of radiation shielding makes the difference between survival and failure. Martial Outpost transforms the real-world constraints of Martian habitation into an engaging, kid-friendly mission simulator for the astronauts of tomorrow.

How it works:

  1. Martian Colony Scenarios & Crises: Players face a dynamic sequence of authentic Mars settlement events and hazards.
  2. Strategic Decision-Making: For every event, players evaluate different courses of action, weighing the risks and trade-offs for the colony before committing to a choice.
  3. Balancing Four Vital Meters: Every decision dynamically shifts Energy, Food, Water, and Radiation levels in real time. If any of the first three drop to zero, or if radiation maxes out, the colony fails to survive.
  4. Contextual Scientific Learning: By interacting with colony events, resource gauges, and the consequences of their choices, players discover and master new scientific terms woven directly into the gameplay and UI—no dry textbooks required.

Benefits & Impact: The primary impact of Martial Outpost is democratizing space literacy and sparking early STEM curiosity through active, experiential learning:

  • Systems & Critical Thinking: Kids quickly grasp that no resource exists in isolation inside a Martian habitat; boosting water or power output might require surface operations—increasing radiation exposure—or drain other vital supplies.
  • Organic Scientific Vocabulary Acquisition: By linking technical terms to clear visual feedback and immediate gameplay outcomes, young players retain concepts effortlessly.
  • Connection to Real Mars Exploration: Prepares the next generation to understand the actual challenges future astronauts will face in NASA's Moon to Mars architecture.

Technology Stack:

  • Game Engine: Godot Engine (4.7.2), utilizing its node architecture, signals, and scene system to manage Martian colony states and UI feedback.
  • Programming Languages: GDScript for decision-tree logic, real-time resource calculations, and dynamic planetary event triggers.
  • Version Control & Collaboration: Git and GitHub for collaborative development, code reviews, and project tracking.

Creativity & Innovation: The innovation of our project lies in translating the real-world challenges of surviving on Mars—such as the lack of magnetic radiation shielding and closed-loop resource management—into a fast-paced, visual decision-making loop tailored for children. Rather than treating planetary science as a multiple-choice quiz, we made the physics of Martian survival the core narrative engine: kids don't just memorize definitions—they experience firsthand why managing radiation and life-support resources is essential to saving their colony.

Team Considerations: Because our target audience is children, every design decision was guided by three core questions:

  • Is it intuitive? We built a clean interface centered on four clear visual meters (Energy, Food, Water, and Radiation) with instant feedback so kids can jump straight into running their Mars colony.
  • Is it educational without feeling like homework? We embedded scientific vocabulary directly into mission choices and brief Martian event descriptions, encouraging learning by doing.
  • Does it encourage replayability? The delicate balance between resources and Martian environmental hazards challenges players to test new strategies on every run, fostering curiosity and experimentation.
